title: Kenya Wildlife Service installs AI-enabled FLIR thermal cameras at Solio, Lake Nakuru and Ol Pejeta to send intrusion alerts to rhino rangers
summary: KWS installed AI-enabled FLIR thermal cameras at three black rhino sites by Sept 2024 (US State Department and WWF funding); intrusion alerts only; no AI-linked arrest or prevented event documented.
account: Citizen Digital reported on 21 September 2024 that the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS), with support from the US Department of State Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs and WWF, had installed FLIR thermal cameras at three black rhino sites, Solio Game Reserve, Lake Nakuru National Park and Ol Pejeta Conservancy, with Solio the latest and Meru National Park named as the next site. Geoffrey Chege of WWF-Kenya said the cameras 'have inbuilt analytics that send out automated alerts every time they detect an intrusion from humans, vehicles or wildlife', and Colby Loucks of WWF-US said the cameras 'can tell you when a human is in the picture or an animal' and alert rangers. KWS Director General Dr Erustus Kanga said: 'I am aware that over the last six years, we have not lost a single black rhino in this sanctuary', a record that predates the Solio installation. The article reports no arrest, interception or prevented poaching event attributable to the cameras; the date used is the article's publication date.
purpose: Automated night-time detection of human and vehicle intrusion at rhino sanctuaries to alert rangers; the claimed benefit is the intended one.
system: Teledyne FLIR thermal cameras with on-board AI analytics for human, vehicle and animal classification and automated ranger alerts

General benefit; Kenya's reduced poaching figures cited in the article are not linked to the cameras.

ai_role.statement: The fetched article (a single news report, Citizen Digital, 21 September 2024) describes AI analytics that classify humans, vehicles and animals in thermal video and send automated alerts to rangers; the statements come from WWF and KWS officials at the handover ceremony. No alert, arrest or prevented poaching event is attributed to the system in any fetched source, so the AI's contribution to rhino protection is unassessed in outcome terms.
